title: Interpret sampling distribution results in context
body: The mean, standard deviation, and probabilities for a sampling distribution of a sample proportion should be interpreted in the context of a specific population.
caution: Say clearly whether you mean the population, one sample of values, or the sample proportion across repeated samples. A vague "it" or "larger samples have less variability" can be read as the wrong one.
ced_evidence: 3.2.C.1 "should be interpreted in the context of a specific population"

title: Conclusion wording for a hypothesis test
body: State the conclusion in context, consistent with and in terms of the alternative hypothesis, using non-definitive language. A one-proportion test conclusion refers to the parameter and the population (3.7.B.6); a two-proportion test conclusion refers to the parameters and the populations (3.13.C.3); a chi-square test conclusion refers to the population(s) (3.15.D.3).
caution: Never say "accept" or "prove" the null hypothesis. A large p-value means there is not convincing evidence for the alternative, which is different from evidence for the null. For chi-square tests, say the data do not provide convincing evidence of an association or a difference, rather than saying there is none.
ced_evidence: 3.7.B.6 "stated in context consistent with, and in terms of, the alternative hypothesis using non-definitive language"; 3.7.B.4; 3.13.C.3; 3.15.D.3

title: Standard error of \hat{p}_1 - \hat{p}_2
